title: Benchmark lineage store, pairwise comparison UI, and auto-triage workflow
creator: Connor Li
description:
Problem: Our current benchmark artifacts are fragmented: raw run outputs live in S3 blobs, summary rows live in a ClickHouse table, and diffs are computed ad-hoc in notebooks. This makes forensic triage slow (30+ minutes to assemble context) and error-prone for regressions in tokens/sec and p95 latencies across model versions and sequence-length distributions.

Goal: Build a durable, queryable benchmark lineage store that captures per-run samples and metadata, expose a pairwise comparison UI that highlights deltas across selected runs/variants, and ship an automated triage workflow that produces prioritized hypotheses (e.g., kernel change, batch sizing, kv-cache eviction) with links to reproducible playback runs. The feature should reduce median triage time from ~30m to <8m for P1 regression alerts and enable on-call to generate a repeatable investigation artifact in one click.
acceptance_criteria: A lineage store exists that stores per-request samples (token timestamps, p95 windows, tokens/sec) with run metadata (model, git-hash, hardware, batch-config, sequence-length histogram).
Pairwise comparison UI: users can select any two runs and see a delta waterfall for tokens/sec, p95, and error-rate with histograms and example input IDs that regressed.
Automated triage: when a regression alert fires, the system creates a triage card with top-3 probable causes, matching diffs (e.g., quantization change), and links to a pre-configured playback job.
Storage cost remains within expected budget: new lineage storage incremental cost < 12% of current benchmarking budget via compression + retention policy.
Runbook: on-call can mark a triage card as "investigating" and assign a follow-up ticket which includes the exact playback config.
design_decisions: Store compressed per-request time-series as Parquet files partitioned by run_id + model + date on S3, with a Postgres/Materialized view for metadata indexing to support fast UI queries.
Use a precomputed comparison cache (pairwise deltas) computed nightly for the active 90-day window to keep UI latency low; invalidate cache on new baseline runs.
Triage ML heuristics: lightweight rule-based scorers (fingerprint mismatches, kernel tag diffs, hardware changes) first; reserve ML classifier for future iteration when labeled triages exist.
Front-end will reuse existing bench catalog components but add a dedicated "Compare" canvas with timeline scrubber and example trace viewer.
tradeoffs: Parquet+S3 vs ClickHouse: Parquet reduces cost and long-term durability but increases query complexity; mitigated by an indexing metadata layer and precomputed caches.
Precompute cache increases nightly batch load and storage but gives interactive UI performance; acceptable for the 90-day active window.
Rule-based triage is faster to ship and explainable but will have lower precision than a trained model; plan to collect labels from usage for future model training.
technical_notes: Schema: run_id, sample_index, timestamp_ms, token_delta, cumulative_tokens, latency_ms, seq_len, input_hash, model, git_hash, kernel_tags, hardware, batch_size, kv_cache_hit_rate.
Retention: keep full samples 30 days, aggregated hourly summaries 365 days. Store full samples in zstd-compressed Parquet; rollup to ORC for long-term if cost requires.
Index service: Postgres table `bench_runs` with JSONB metadata (small), materialized views for quick list queries. Use primary key run_id.
Playback job: airflow DAG that accepts run_id pair and replays deterministic request set with fixed env to reproduce p95/tokens/sec deltas.

rollout_plan: Canary: enable lineage store + compare UI for internal bench users (team: infra, eng) for 1 week.
Stage: open to all internal users and enable automated triage for non-critical alerts for 2 weeks.
GA: enable triage creation on P1 alerts and notify on-call after 30 days of successful canary metrics.
monitoring_and_alerting: Alert if ingestion lag > 5 minutes for active runs
Alert if precompute job fails 3 times in a row
Dashboard: UI latency P50/P95 for pairwise compare under 500ms for cached queries
Regression detection: fire only when delta p95 > 10% and tokens/sec drop > 8% (configurable)
